questions.stem: This child with severe thalassemia has a prominent, bossed forehead. What process most directly produces this skeletal change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Expansion of the marrow cavity from erythroid hyperplasia driven by ineffective erythropoiesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Iron deposition within the cranial bones

explanation.summary: Ineffective erythropoiesis drives massive marrow hyperplasia; in severe thalassemia the marrow expands the skull and facial bones, producing frontal bossing, malar prominence, and maxillary hypertrophy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ineffective erythropoiesis drives massive marrow hyperplasia; in severe thalassemia the marrow expands the skull and facial bones, producing frontal bossing, malar prominence, and maxillary hypertrophy.
